memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Balaam saw Amalek and spoke his message: "Amalek was first among the nations, but their end will be utter destruction." Then he saw the Kenites and spoke his message: "Your dwelling place is secure, your nest is set in a rock; yet you Kenites will be destroyed when Ashur takes you captive." - Num 24:20-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's gaze turns to other nations. Amalek, once first among the nations, would come to utter ruin. The Kenites had built their nest securely in the rock, seemingly safe, yet even they would one day be carried off into captivity. No earthly security, however solid it appeared, could guarantee lasting safety.

There is a sobering pattern in these words. Nations that seemed strong and established were destined to fall. The Kenites felt secure in their rocky heights, but rock and stronghold could not save them from God's appointed judgment. Human security is always more fragile than it looks.

This speaks to our own tendency to build our lives on things that feel solid but cannot last. We construct our nests of wealth, status, achievement, or reputation, imagining they will keep us safe. Yet everything built on earthly foundations is subject to decay and loss. Only what is founded on God endures.

Where, then, is true security found? Not in any earthly stronghold, but in the God who is our rock and refuge. In Christ we have a foundation that cannot be shaken, a hope that outlasts every kingdom and every crisis (Matt 7:24-25). Build your life on Him, the only rock that will never crumble beneath you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "secure nests" are you tempted to trust that cannot truly last?
2. How does the fall of seemingly strong nations warn you today?
3. What does it mean to build your life on Christ, the unshakable rock?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from trusting in earthly securities that cannot last. Be my rock and refuge, and help me build my life on Christ, the only foundation that will never crumble. Amen.
